board.name: The Inverted Yield Curve
board.question: Is the curve inverted, and what followed when it was?

headline.label: Not inverted
headline.detail: 10y−3m +0.87 pp on Sep 4, 2026 · positive for 222 trading days
headline.rule: The curve is inverted when the 10-year yield sits below the 3-month yield, so the spread is negative.

board.name: Has Housing Rolled Over?
board.question: Has housing rolled over, and how early does it turn?

headline.label: No rollover signal
headline.detail: starts 1,239k SAAR, 27% below their Apr 2022 peak · single-family −8.3% year on year
headline.rule: The rollover signal is on when the 3-month average of single-family starts sits 20% or more below its level a year earlier.

board.name: Are Credit Spreads Blowing Out?
board.question: Are spreads blowing out, and when they did, what followed?

headline.label: No blowout
headline.detail: Baa−Aaa 0.44 pp, at its two-year low · NFCI −0.56
headline.rule: The blowout signal is on when the 3-month average of the Baa minus Aaa spread sits 0.40 percentage points or more above its low over the prior two years.

board.name: Are Banks Tightening?
board.question: Are banks tightening, and what has followed when they did?

headline.label: Standards neutral
headline.rule: The tightening signal is on when the net percentage of banks tightening C&I standards for large firms is at or above +20.

board.name: Is Freight Moving?
board.question: Is freight moving, and does it warn?

headline.label: Freight moving
headline.detail: tonnage +0.6% year over year (3-month average) · rail carloads +2.0%
headline.rule: The freight-contraction signal is on when the 3-month average of truck tonnage sits below its level a year earlier.

board.name: Is the Consumer Holding Up?
board.question: Does what consumers say match what they do?

headline.label: Sentiment slumped, spending growing
headline.detail: sentiment 55.2 (bottom 3% since 1952) · real spending +2.1% year over year
headline.rule: The slump signal is on when the average of the last three sentiment readings sits 15 percent or more below its best such average over the prior two years. The label names the say-do gap: which of the two halves, what they say and what they do, is currently weak.

board.name: Is the Economy Producing?
board.question: Is the economy producing, and does output warn or confirm?

headline.label: Output expanding
headline.detail: industrial production 103.0, +1.1% year over year, 1.1% below its record
headline.rule: A downturn is a stretch where the 3-month average of industrial production sits at least 3 percent below its highest such average over the prior two years, for at least three months in a row; stretches separated by fewer than nine clear months merge into one. Each downturn is dated two ways: the CREST, the highest average in the two years before it began, and the ALARM, the first month past the threshold. An NBER peak from eighteen months before the alarm to twelve months after the last signalling month is assigned to the nearest downturn; the window is wider behind than ahead because production keeps sliding well into a recession before it clears any threshold. Lead time is reported from both clocks, and both are expected to be flat or negative: industrial production is one of the series the dating committee itself watches, so it confirms a recession rather than predicting one. A crest window reaching before January 1919 renders as left-censored.

board.name: A Century of Work
board.question: What has unemployment actually done, over a century?

headline.label: Sahm rule clear
headline.detail: Sahm at −0.07 against the 0.50 trigger, unemployment 4.1% · clear for 22 months
headline.rule: The Sahm rule fires when the 3-month average unemployment rate sits 0.50 points or more above its lowest 3-month average of the prior twelve months.

board.name: Debt Atlas
board.question: How much does everyone owe, against what record?

headline.label: Above the WWII peak
headline.detail: gross debt 122.6% of GDP against 119.1% in 1946 · held by the public 98.7%, still below its own 106.3% record
headline.rule: Gross federal debt exceeds its 1946 wartime peak of 119.1% of GDP (FRED GFDGDPA188S). Debt held by the public is scored against its own 1946 peak of 106.3% (FRED FYPUGDA188S); the two records sit thirteen points apart and are never quoted across each other.

board.name: Diesel Crack Spread
board.question: What is it worth to turn a barrel into diesel?

headline.label: Margins historically wide
headline.detail: US crack $96.70 on a 4-week average, 99th percentile since 1986
headline.rule: Margins read as historically wide when the 4-week average US crack sits at or above the 90th percentile of every daily observation on record.
